title: What each arranger contributed
summary: Hawkins describes how Lowe, Johnson and Kirkland arranged and how he left it to them.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Yeah. Well, you sure have a good memory. I mean, that's for sure.
I had a few outsides, you know. But, when it's like the primary, all the arranging was done right there in the band. You know?

Right. Are there any significant things that you would want to share with us about the things done by this crew of arrangers you had? In terms of either the things that you liked a great deal, or specific stylistic things that were there. How they differed, or similarities. Or, how they contributed to the collective sound of the band.
Well, all of them had, did their part. And then you say, they had different sounds. They had different ways like Sam had his way of making his arrangement in his
sound or his style that he wanted. But, Bill Johnson, he had a certain way, like bringing in vocals along with his subtleties of his sound.

Leroy Kirkland. He used to arrange his tunes by giving us and make this arrangement for me, and do it this way or this way. But, and then we'd sit down some time at the piano until he found out what I wanted and he would do it that way. And then sometimes, he would bring it not the way I asked for it. But, I liked it. So, I let it stay that way, you know, cause I didn't go against them cause they had the feeling that I wanted. It seemed like they knew me better than I knew myself. Knew what I wanted, you know.

So, I didn't have too much to say about the arrangement after they got them in there once they asked me a few questions if they wanted to at that time when I said we gonna do this. And when they brought in their original tunes, they knew just about what I wanted. So, I could concern myself about playing, you
know. So, they would do that and I didn't have too much less to do about it.
